title: 5 Secrets to the Perfect Cake Every Time
excerpt: After years of baking, these are the tips I wish someone told me from the start.
content:
From My Kitchen to Yours

Baking is both an art and a science. After years of experimenting, failing, and perfecting, I have learned a few things that transformed my cakes from good to unforgettable.

Here are my top 5 secrets:

1. Room Temperature Ingredients

This is the number one mistake most people make. Your butter, eggs, and milk should all be at room temperature before you start. Cold ingredients do not mix well and can result in a lumpy batter and an uneven cake.

2. Do Not Overmix

Once you add the flour, mix until just combined. Overmixing develops gluten, which makes your cake tough instead of tender. A few lumps in the batter are perfectly fine!

3. Invest in Good Vanilla

Please, put down the artificial vanilla extract. Real vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste makes a world of difference. Your taste buds will thank you.

4. The Toothpick Test is Your Best Friend

Insert a toothpick into the center of your cake. If it comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs, your cake is done. Wet batter means it needs more time.

5. Let It Cool Completely

I know it is tempting, but do not frost a warm cake. It will melt your frosting and create a mess. Let your cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack until completely cool.

Follow these tips and you will be baking like a pro in no time. And if you want to skip the baking and let me do it for you - check out my cakes page!
